event.active_blue_east_blue_01_baratie_s: {{npc_rohan}} wipes his hands, checks your crew capacity, and accepts a berth aboard.
You pay for the dishes prepared for the passing crew.
{{npc_rohan}} trades schedules, cargo talk, and customer rumors without promising to leave.
At Baratie, {{npc_rohan}} finishes a service for a crew that has just left him without a berth. His knives are packed; his bag is already tied.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_beach_wre: You refuse to decide who owns what the sea threw back.
You assign the wreck to the wrong flag and trigger an expensive dispute.
You also identify the last repair, recent enough to trace the owner.
The marks remain ambiguous and nobody yields the cargo.
You find the yard mark and hull number beneath the weed.
Both groups accuse you of favoring the other and keep everything.
The split is clean enough that both sides pay you.
You get a truce but no clear split.
The fishers and merchant accept a written split.
A small wreck has washed onto an East Blue beach. Fishers are already pulling planks free while a merchant claims to recognize the cargo.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_clinic_tr: A merchant captain sells medical stores at a steep price.
Buy from a ship
{{npc_ari}} agrees to come aboard after finishing the shift.
Offer {{npc_ari}} a berth
Sheets become bandages clean enough to last the night.
Sacrifice clean cloth
Calm returns, but {{npc_ari}} is holding the last clean roll. Two patients are still bleeding, and port supplies will not arrive before dawn.
The Last Bandage
An argument breaks out and overturns a treatment tray.
The whole room follows your directions until help arrives.
The crowd quiets a little but keeps crowding {{npc_ari}}.
Families step back and finally leave a lane for emergencies.
Calm the room
You empty the clean-linen cabinets and bring supplies to the treatment tables.
Fetch supplies
You prioritize badly and a minor injury takes the last useful dose.
You even establish a clean flow to prevent cross-infection.
You stabilize the line, but too slowly to prevent shortages.
You separate emergencies, fractures, and simple wounds before {{npc_ari}} runs out of hands.
Triage the injured
A dock collision floods the local clinic at once. {{npc_ari}} no longer has enough hands to sort injuries, panicked families, and vanishing supplies.
The Clinic Overflows
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_coastal_t: You leave the fake toll behind.
Bin the notice
Port authorities refund part of what you paid.
Claim your payment back
Your account completes the amounts and descriptions of the gang.
Send your account
Three months later, a notice circulates through East Blue ports: the fake toll has been broken up. Victims are now comparing their receipts.
The Impossible Receipt
You keep the clipping as proof that a small racket can leave a lasting trail.
Keep the clipping
You let the story close with the newspaper.
Move on
Three months after the notice, a short gazette confirms the racketeers were convicted. The copied receipts were enough to link their boats.
The False Toll Falls
The men laugh and double the fee while pointing weapons.
Two rowers realize they have no official cover and stop following.
They lower the price a little but keep the racket.
Their leader backs down when you ask which office signed their order.
Call their bluff
You cut too close to a shoal and scrape the hull before escaping.
You even pin them in your lee before breaking away.
You outrun them, but only after straining the rig.
You take a wind they cannot hold and leave them behind.
Outmaneuver them
You pay their “toll” and continue without a fight.
Pay the toll
An armed skiff cuts across your path and demands a toll “for the coast.” It carries neither kingdom flag nor Marine insignia.
The Flagless Toll
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_coastwatc: You compare cargoes and ringing times, then ask to be written if the pattern returns.
Follow the ledgers
You help restore the station and promise to answer their news.
Join the watch
You refuse to pick a side but leave a way to reach you.
Leave a contact
Under the bell, the clapper bears two marks: an old crack and a fresh cut. The keepers split between repairing the station and investigating false signals.
The Split Clapper
Several ports receive the times and cargo marks.
Circulate the pattern
The keepers keep recording without warning the broker.
Keep it quiet
Merchants pay to receive suspicious timings before departure.
Sell the warning to merchants
A year later, the ledgers arrive by courier. The false rings now follow the same three cargoes, all insured by the same broker.
The First Year’s Books
The money pays for rope, oil, and fittings for the season.
Send Berrys
Your notes reach both neighboring posts with repair plans.
Share their method
The keepers begin coordinating watches instead of maintaining three full teams.
Propose a shared watch
A year later, a letter from the keepers finds you: the bell works, but two neighboring posts have gone silent for lack of money and hands.
The First Season
You propose that major merchants fund upkeep in exchange for detailed reports.
Fund it by subscription
You ask the three stations to remain a simple coastal chain instead of growing too fast.
Keep it local
You urge the stations to share schedules, failures, and warnings freely with every port.
Open the network
Thirty months after your first visit, a letter recounts the storm: three stations rang together and an entire convoy changed course in time. The keepers ask how the network should develop.
The Three-Bell Storm
Several ports contribute a small fixed share to upkeep.
Accept port dues
You back a public collection and the network stays open to everyone.
Keep it free
The keepers keep your contact but now make decisions without you.
Step back
Two years later, a gazette prints the free network schedule. Fishers use it as much as large cargo ships, but donations barely cover repairs.
The Open Bells
You back keepers who now send the same warning to every ship.
Equalize the alerts
Companies keep priority and fund rapid expansion.
Honor the contracts
Danger warnings become public; only commercial reports stay paid.
Split the service
Two years later, subscriptions have paid for new bells. But small boats complain they receive warnings after the companies funding the network.
The Contract Bells
Each station keeps its own rules but shares emergency signals with the others.
Let each coast decide
The network writes public safety ahead of every commercial contract.
Safety before profit
The network reserves enough income to depend on no kingdom or company.
A self-funded watch
Years after the first bell, three veteran keepers write together. Their chain now covers several East Blue coasts and needs one common principle before expanding further.
The Keepers Return
The keepers send you a share from their recognition fund.
Accept their stipend
You refuse signature and money: the chain now belongs to those who ring it.
Leave the legacy to them
Your name joins those who shaped East Blue’s watch chain.
Sign their charter
Nearly ten years after your first visit, a letter bears the mark of several coastal stations. The old bell still exists, but it is no longer alone.
The Bell You Hear Everywhere
You put down enough money to restore the bell before the next night.
Fund a repair
The bracket breaks under your test and the bell drops into the sand.
You also identify why the corrosion returns every season.
You find the crack too late to stop the clapper failing.
You spot a worn pin nobody could see from the beach.
Inspect the bell
You mix up two different nights and accuse an innocent fisher.
You even link the false rings to an old coastal smuggling route.
You confirm the false signals without finding who causes them.
The times reveal someone rings just before certain cargo ships pass.
Compare the reports
On an East Blue coast, an old warning bell sometimes rings with no ship in danger—then stays silent when real fog comes in.
The Coastwatch Bell
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_cocoyasi_: Planks and chain hold the gate until repairs.
Brace it with scrap
A carpenter replaces the hinge before the next tide.
Pay a carpenter
Families move tools and harvests before the next tide.
Warn the lower fields
Water returns, but a small side gate remains open toward the lower fields. If it breaks, the next tide will flood them again.
The Second Gate
You help farmers save the nearest plants without fixing the canal.
Carry water by hand
The gate gives at once and the timber slams your side.
You also brace the split beam before it can fall again.
You free it halfway; water runs, but tears out a bank.
The gate rises and fresh water returns to the canal.
Lift the gate
You open the wrong ditch and salt water pushes in faster.
You also work out why the tide blocks the canal every week.
You find the blockage, but only after losing part of the flow.
You find a flap jammed beneath weeds and clear it.
Trace the blockage
In Cocoyasi Village, irrigation stops as the tide rises. The first ditches already taste of salt, and farmers run toward the gate.
The Salted Channel
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_contraban: The vials sink. The skiff immediately vanishes behind the swell.
Dump the vials
You keep the abbreviations in mind and throw the vials overboard.
Memorize the list
You signal for them to take the bundle back. They refuse and pull away.
Signal the skiff
The bundle holds unmarked vials and a list of abbreviated ports. A dark skiff stays just close enough to watch what you do.
The Bundle Opened
You send enough Berrys to close the debt without endorsing their trade.
Pay them off
Your silence becomes an answer; they promise to remember your name.
Send nothing
You send back the copied abbreviations with one line: “Change your route.”
Send their list back
Six months later, a note slipped under a door bears the same tarred knot: “You owe us a bundle, or an explanation.”
The Black Knot
The trade stops being your concern.
Forget them
You keep the knot pattern in mind for future docks.
Keep watching
You let the small war end without hunting the last smugglers.
Take the win
A year after the bundle, an East Blue gazette reports several smuggling skiffs have left those same ports. The black knot stops appearing.
A Route Abandoned
The blade slips and the swell slams you against the hull.
You also recover the marked knot that identifies the gang.
You cut one line, but the bundle remains caught under the rudder.
The bundle comes free before it can damage the rudder.
Cut it free
You leave the bundle alone while it does not threaten the rudder.
Hold course
You follow a false trace and hit floating debris.
You also catch its hooded lamp behind a swell.
The wake fades before you can link the bundle to a boat.
You pick out the small wake of a boat that just left your stern.
Find their wake
A dull thump hits beneath your ship. A tarred bundle is tied to the rudder, planted overnight without anyone boarding.
Below the Waterline
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_crew_noti: {{npc_owen}} inspects your hull for a day’s wage and leaves you a repair list.
You note departures, full crews, and the berths still open.
{{npc_owen}} hears your offer, checks the available berth, and accepts a place aboard.
In an East Blue port, {{npc_owen}} removes his notice from the crew board: his previous captain sailed without paying for repairs.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_dockyard_: You spread their story among other ports.
Spread the case
You leave them the evidence and step out of the dispute.
Leave them the copy
Your receipt completes their wage case.
Send your receipt
Five months later, a workers’ letter finds you: the copied ledger forced the yard to reopen its accounts. One week of wages is still missing.
The Copied Names
Your name remains tied to the case in the yard.
Accept their thanks
For you too, the account is finally closed.
Close the book
The worker returns what you fronted.
Take back your advance
Ten months after the first ledger, the workers report that the yard paid the balance and now posts hours before each payday.
The Closed Account
You copy the crossed-out names before the foreman closes the ledger.
Copy the missing names
You front one worker’s wage and keep the receipt.
Pay one worker
You refuse to sign a ledger you did not keep.
Refuse the dispute
In an East Blue shipyard, six workers wait for wages. The foreman shows a ledger where their names were crossed out the night before.
The Wage Book
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_fish_mark: You demand a share of the repayments in exchange for your testimony.
Demand a cut
You refuse to prolong the matter. The thread ends for you.
Drop the matter
Your account joins the case built by cheated merchants.
Send your testimony
Four months later, an East Blue letter arrives: the rigged scale has moved from market to market, and several sellers are now blaming one another.
The Same Scale
The settlement includes a small payment for witnesses who helped establish the fraud.
Accept the witness payment
The news leaves with the paper.
Move on
You keep proof that one small rule changed.
Keep the clipping
An East Blue gazette finally reports the settlement: merchants caught with false weights repay customers, and markets now display reference weights.
The Stalls’ Judgment
The vendor pockets your money and promises to fix the weights—a weak promise.
Buy the vendor’s silence
Customers compare baskets. The vendor folds his awning under jeers.
Call out the stall
You discreetly mark the true weight under the tray, leaving proof for later customers.
Mark the scale
At the fish market, an old customer taps two identical weights: one rings hollow. The vendor is already trying to pack away his scale.
Hollow Weights
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_fishing_n: Your shipwright braces the winch; the fisher gets free without sacrificing the whole net.
Brace the winch
The tension drops and the fisher stays aboard, but a morning catch escapes.
Cut the net
Several hands pull the fisher free of the line before the winch starts again.
Haul him back
The net survives the crossing, then its winch jams. A fisher is caught by the ankle and slides toward the rail while the shoal pulls the other end.
The Winch Jams
You mistake a submerged float for a gap and pull the net against the bow.
You also spot the winch straining abnormally on the leeward fishing boat.
You avoid the main net, but a side line wraps beneath the hull.
The floats reveal the net pocket before it closes your passage.
Read the floats
You kill your speed and let the fishers open a lane.
Slow down and hail
The keel catches the lead line; the net whips the rudder before tearing free.
You cross without touching a mesh and even signal the current to the fishers.
You clear the net, but floats hammer the hull and tear one line loose.
You read the net drift and pass through its only opening.
Thread the gap
At dawn, two East Blue fishing boats close a channel with a huge, nearly invisible net. Your bow is coming fast as the floats vanish under a short swell.
The Net Across the Channel
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_fog_bell_: The skiff is free, but the marker will stay silent until repaired.
Cut the chain
You keep distance and guide a towboat to him once the fog lifts.
Mark his position
You pull the skiff free of the chain and the bell starts ringing again.
Tow him clear
Near the marker, a keeper struggles in a small skiff: the bell chain has fouled beneath his keel.
The Marker Skiff
You anchor clear of the breakers and wait for the fog to open a path.
Anchor until clear
You mistake an echo and advance toward rock.
You also hear a small metal hammer near the marker.
You avoid the first rock, but the second scrapes the planking.
The rhythm of breakers sketches the coast through the fog.
Listen for breakers
The bottom rises faster than expected and the keel touches.
You find both the channel and the exact position of the silent marker.
You find the channel, but only after scraping a shoal.
The soundings trace a safe channel despite the silent bell.
Sound the depth
Fog swallows the East Blue coast and the reef bell stays silent. Each wave throws a different echo off unseen rocks.
The Silent Fog Bell
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_goa_gate_: Nobody passes until the guards drop the surcharge.
Block the gate
The chain rises and the cart passes before the fee changes again.
Cover their passage
You leave the gate with the duplicate ledger numbers in mind.
Leave with the proof
A servants’ cart remains blocked despite the commotion. Guards demand one more fee before lifting the chain.
The Servants’ Cart
The crowd turns on you when guards threaten to close the gate.
Even a palace officer demands the ledger after hearing the crowd.
Counting resumes, but the poorest carts remain blocked.
The clerk recounts in public and several surcharges vanish.
Demand a public count
You pay only your own line and pass the gate.
Pay your line
You search the wrong cart and the guards charge you for the delay.
You find the column reserving exemptions for wealthy crests.
You see the discrepancies, but the clerk closes the book before you can prove them.
You spot the same goods charged twice under different names.
Find the duplicate ledger
At a gate in Goa Kingdom, modest carts pay twice while crested carriages pass through. A clerk hides a second ledger beneath the desk.
The Gate Ledger
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_harbor_qu: You learn he paid a sailor to leave an island without telling his family.
Hear his story
You buy him a meal before the adults decide what happens next.
Buy him a meal
Port authorities register him before investigating who brought him aboard.
Turn him over to the port
During the examination, a teenager emerges from a side hold. He is not sick, but nobody listed him on the ship’s manifest.
The Hidden Passenger
The cordon breaks and the crowd floods the gangway.
Dockworkers and families organize their own line away from the gangway.
You keep the crowd out, but rumors are already spreading through the port.
You win enough calm for the clinic to examine the crew.
Hold the cordon
You misread the signs and needlessly expose several dockers.
You even trace the cause to a badly stored fish barrel.
You rule out the worst, but too late to prevent panic.
You recognize food poisoning, not a contagious fever.
Inspect the symptoms
You stay behind the rope until the official diagnosis.
Respect quarantine
A merchant ship docks under a yellow flag. Three sailors are vomiting on deck while families and dockworkers already crowd the cordon.
The Yellow Flag
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_loguetown: The yard releases a dinghy and records the sale.
The yard prepares a sloop for your departure.
You leave with prices, visible flaws, and no debt.
In Loguetown, a shipyard displays several hulls ready to sail. The foreman knocks on each plank and calls out prices to buyers.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_marine_ch: You refuse to become the owner’s guarantor.
Let the owner answer
You quote the posted fee in front of the soldiers. Several eyes leave the deputy.
Name the false fee
You pay to move the line and remember the deputy’s face.
Pay to clear the line
A crate opens: nothing illegal, only food already taxed. The deputy still holds out his hand to the owner.
The Open Crate
The officer cuts you off and seizes a crate as an “inspection fee.”
Dockworkers repeat your figures loudly enough to draw the post commander.
You get a regular inspection, but only after a made-up fine.
The soldiers return to the official manifest and stop the extractions.
Press the manifest
You accuse the wrong man and the inspection turns hostile.
You also spot the second ledger hidden under the table.
You see the tension, but not its source before the crates are opened.
You spot the deputy diverting every crate before it reaches the ledger.
Read the officer
You let the crates be opened one by one without provoking the post.
Submit to the search
At an East Blue coastal post, Marines hold a line of cargo. A deputy demands “inspection fees” absent from the official manifest.
The Crate Inspection
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_marine_pa: You help the clerk close cleanly and send the crowd to the next service.
You front enough to feed one recruit and keep the receipt for tomorrow.
You sort the sheets by unit; the missing pay records surface before closing.
At an East Blue Marine office, the pay shutter comes down with a dozen sailors still waiting. The clerk says one ledger is missing and refuses to reopen the cashbox.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_market_br: You keep onlookers from pocketing the fallen rolls until the merchant returns.
You keep a small payment for securing the safe.
You leave guards and merchants to handle their money.
A cart snaps an axle in the market. A small safe springs open on impact, and rolls of Berrys scatter between boots.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_merchant_: You keep contact with the convoy.
Answer the merchants
You offer to escort them again when routes cross.
Ask for work
You thank them and leave the convoy to its routes.
Close the correspondence
Nine months later, a convoy letter finds you: the delayed captain survived, and the merchants remember the slot you held—or refused.
Nine Months After the Squall
You send the money back to the ship that took the worst damage.
Send it back
The payment arrives with the accounts.
Take the share
You refuse the share but leave your name in their ledger of reliable captains.
Refuse money, keep the name
A second letter arrives with the yearly accounts: the convoy opened a steadier route and pays those who helped during its worst crossing.
The Convoy Share
You refuse to join a formation you do not know.
Keep your own route
You pass your heading to the lost ship without joining formation.
Share your heading
You close the convoy gap until the delayed ship returns.
Take the empty slot
An East Blue merchant convoy crosses your course with an empty slot in the middle. The missing ship flashes far behind, separated by a squall.
The Convoy Gap
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_mirrorbal: You hold the batten until everyone clears the stage.
Hold the batten
You leave the technicians to recover their stage.
Leave backstage
The performers bow in front of the fallen curtain as if it were planned.
Make it the finale
The mechanism moves again, then a second rope snaps: the curtain drops behind the performers instead of in front of them.
The Curtain Drops
The batten spins and throws you into the scenery.
You realign the whole rig without stopping the music.
You stop the curtain, but tear the main backdrop.
You free the pulley before the performers enter.
Climb the rig
The curtain drops cleanly to the floor; the show continues without scenery.
Cut the curtain
Your diversion turns into a commotion and seats break.
The crowd even calls for your name before the performers return.
The crowd grumbles until the stage resumes.
You turn the wait into a game and keep the room with you.
Hold the crowd
On Mirrorball Island, the main curtain jams above a full stage. The metal batten shudders while the audience is already stamping its feet.
The Jammed Curtain
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_night_anc: The anchor bites again and the ship stops drifting.
You choose to drift offshore rather than risk a broken chain.
Everyone takes a station until the bottom is safe again.
At night anchorage, the coast slowly grows closer instead of staying fixed. The anchor is dragging while the wind turns toward the rocks.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_night_wat: You force the saboteurs to dump their lantern before fleeing.
Chase the boat
The decoy sinks with its lenses.
Destroy the false light
You keep course and pass the position to the next port.
Mark the position
Along the reef, you spot a small boat beneath the false lantern. Someone is already folding the signal light to disappear.
One Light Too Many
You stop advancing until the coast can be read.
Heave to
You mistake a reflection for the main signal and guide the ship toward shoals.
You even read the deliberate offset between the lamps and spot the trap.
You read the code too late; the hull scrapes a tongue of rock.
You separate the true light from the decoy and correct course.
Read the light pattern
The swell fools you in the dark; a hard impact runs up the keel.
You cut behind the reef and come up leeward of the false signal.
You avoid the worst, but a rock tears away planks.
The swell reveals the safe channel despite the lamps.
Read the swell
Two coastal lanterns flash opposite instructions ahead of your ship. Behind them, close to shore, the sea breaks white over an unseen reef.
Two Lights in the Dark
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_orange_to: Passersby move under awnings; the sign falls without hitting anyone.
The owner pays for a quick repair rather than closing the shop.
You lash the sign against the wall before it falls into the street.
In Orange Town, a gust tears two bolts from a large shop sign. It swings over a street still crowded with customers.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_poster_mi: The printer crosses out the wrong name and promises a new plate in the next run.
The stack becomes paper strips before the wrong face spreads farther.
You let the confusion run long enough for people to talk about you.
At an East Blue printer, a stack of official notices bears your face beside another traveler’s name. The first copies have already gone out.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_quay_rope: The quay sees the severed strand. The accusation shifts.
Show the cut
You take a few Berrys to close the incident before an inquiry.
Take compensation
You leave the crane before the argument becomes yours.
Leave it to the quay
The foreman immediately blames a young rigger for the bad knot. The boy points to a strand cut clean through, not worn.
Under the Crane
The rope tears your palms and the crate slams into you.
You seize the tackle in one sharp motion and save crate, stall, and dockers.
You slow the crate, but it smashes the neighboring stall.
You lock the rope just before the crate sweeps across the quay.
Catch the line
The crowd backs away. The crate breaks, but nobody is under it.
Clear the quay
You slide too late and the crate corner crushes your shoulder.
You clear the dockers, then guide the crate into a pile of nets.
You shove a docker clear, but the cargo bursts across the stones.
You pull two dockers clear before the crate hits.
Dive under the crate
A tackle snaps above an East Blue quay. A loaded crate swings toward dockworkers while the loose rope lashes across the planks.
The Tackle Snaps
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_rare_anim: You let nature settle the crossing without adding a human danger.
The animal charges and throws you into the ferns.
You even guide the herd around the new nest without spooking it.
You move the nest, but crush several eggs in the panic.
You slide the nest behind a stump before the herd passes.
You strike the wrong trunk and draw the herd toward you.
You find a natural path they take without panic.
The herd turns, but tramples the nest edge.
You use their reactions to sound to divert the herd.
On Rare Animal Island, a bright nest lies in a muddy run. A heavy herd is coming straight toward it, spooked by a crack behind you.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_repair_qu: The yard moves your ship up the queue and starts before the tide.
You help block two hulls and earn a minor repair in return.
You keep your Berrys and accept losing the day at the quay.
An East Blue port yard is packed with damaged hulls. Your ship is still behind three urgent repairs as the tide begins to fall.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_shimotsuk: You bow and leave the mat before pride decides for you.
End the match
The bout becomes brief, precise, and bloodless.
First touch wins
You play for footing rather than blows.
Force the ring-out
After the exchange, the student refuses to rack the shinai: one last point, this time by your rule.
The Last Point
Your pivot catches the mat edge and you fall hard.
You make three attacks miss without leaving the mat.
You evade two grips, then get trapped in the corner.
Your footwork opens the angle and you score cleanly.
Fight on footwork
You drive too hard and tumble off the mat to laughter.
You shut down every reset and control the mat from start to finish.
Your opponent absorbs the push and sends you out.
You hold center and force your opponent backward.
Take the center
You stay at the edge and study the fighters’ mistakes.
Watch the drill
In Shimotsuki Village, a teacher opens the mat to travelers. A student points a shinai at you: one exchange, no grudges.
The Open Mat
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_sixis_wat: Smoke clears the basin long enough to fill containers.
Smoke them out
You take just enough water to leave without disturbing the cave further.
Take one flask
You refuse to risk a sting in the narrow fissure.
Turn back
The fissure drops into a cool pocket. Water is there, but a swarm of insects covers the only reachable basin.
Shade in the Fissure
The sheet tears and you waste the last of your water.
You set several condensation traps before noon.
The rig produces a few mouthfuls, too little to stay long.
Condensation fills enough flasks to keep exploring.
Build a solar still
You keep enough water to reach the coast without pressing farther.
Ration and leave
You follow seabirds toward a dry cliff and lose more water.
You also spot moss marking a reservoir beneath the rock.
You find damp signs, but not enough before the heat.
The morning flight leads you to a damp fissure.
Follow the birds
On Sixis, your last water cask leaks into hot sand. No spring is visible, and the vegetation thickens toward the rocky interior.
The Empty Cask
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_storm_sai: Spars and rope lock the mast step in place.
Brace it now
You set aside enough to replace the fitting when you dock.
Set aside repair money
You keep your stores and accept a fragile rig until port.
Save the materials
The squall passes, but the mast step knocks with every roll. A fitting has shifted, and the next sea could tear it loose.
The Mast Still Shudders
You sacrifice the sail before it can tear out the mast.
Cut the sail loose
A gust tears you from the rigging and the sail splits to the bolt rope.
You reef the sail in the lull of a single gust.
You save the mast, but the sail tears farther.
You choke the sail down before the tear reaches the mast.
Reef by hand
The turn unloads the sail too late and the mast takes the full strain.
You use the squall itself to bear away without punishing the rig.
The heading holds, but the rig groans and loses fittings.
You put the sail in the wind shadow just before the next gust.
Turn under the squall
A fast squall hits broadside. Your mainsail opens down its full height, and every gust now wrenches at the mast.
The Sail Splits
